items.headline: US Futures Mixed as Investors Await Tech Earnings and Fed Decision
items.summary: US stock futures are displaying mixed to lower trends in early trading, reflecting investor caution ahead of a packed week featuring major technology earnings and the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting. Concerns surrounding AI chip demand, rising corporate spending, and persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are contributing to the subdued sentiment. The Federal Reserve is anticipated to begin its meeting today, with markets pricing in a notable chance of an interest rate hike. Not financial advice.

items.headline: OPKO Health surges on strong Q2 and raised guidance
items.summary: OPKO Health shares jumped 9% in pre-market trading after the company reported better-than-expected Q2 revenue and earnings, and subsequently raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance.

items.headline: Celestica gains after exceeding Q2 estimates
items.summary: Celestica saw a 4% increase in pre-market trading, benefiting from strong Q2 revenue and earnings that surpassed analyst expectations, leading to an upgraded FY2026 outlook.

items.headline: Workday extends gains, up 9.0% on Monday
items.summary: Workday continued its upward trajectory, closing Monday with a 9.0% gain, part of a persistent positive trend over several weeks.

items.headline: Aehr Test Systems drops on shelf registration filing
items.summary: Shares of Aehr Test Systems declined 5% in pre-market trading following the company's filing of a mixed shelf registration with the SEC, which investors often view as a potential for future dilution.

items.headline: Universal Health Services cuts guidance, misses earnings
items.summary: Universal Health Services stock fell 4% in pre-market after the hospital operator lowered its FY2026 EPS guidance and reported Q2 earnings below consensus estimates.

items.headline: AI chip stocks slide amid spending and competition concerns
items.summary: Major semiconductor companies like Nvidia, Micron, and Applied Materials saw pre-market declines ranging from 1.1% to 4.6% as investors grow cautious over corporate spending on AI infrastructure and increasing Chinese competition.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Kicks Off Critical Two-Day Policy Meeting
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) commences its fifth meeting of 2026 today, running through Wednesday. Markets are closely watching for any signals regarding interest rate adjustments, with approximately a one-third to 38% probability of a rate hike being priced in. The Committee will focus on inflation risks, including those tied to recent energy disruptions, and Chair Kevin Warsh's guidance on future policy.

items.headline: Big Tech Earnings Set to Drive Market Volatility This Week
items.summary: This week marks a significant period for earnings reports from major technology companies, including Amazon, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and Apple. Investors are keenly focused on these reports for insights into continued spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure and the broader health of the tech sector. Expectations are high, with the semiconductor and information technology sectors projected to lead in Q2 earnings growth.

items.headline: Majority of S&P 500 Stocks Above 50-Day Moving Average
items.summary: For the first time since February, most stocks within the S&P 500 are trading above their 50-day moving average, a technical indicator often seen as a sign of underlying market strength. Approximately 70% of the index's constituents also remain above their 200-day moving average.

items.headline: Apple Stock Significantly Outperforms Nasdaq 100 in July
items.summary: Apple's stock ($AAPL) has demonstrated remarkable performance in July, outperforming the Nasdaq 100 index by 23 percentage points. This strong showing is attributed to a shift in investor sentiment, with Apple's cautious approach to AI now viewed as a strategic advantage rather than a drawback.

items.headline: US Durable Goods Orders Rise Less Than Expected
items.summary: US durable goods orders for Monday rose by 0.3% month-over-month, falling short of the 1.6% expectation. However, core durable capital goods orders showed a stronger increase of 0.9% for the month.

items.headline: Record High Margin Debt Raises Market Alarm
items.summary: Total U.S. stock market margin debt has reached an unprecedented $1.53 trillion, according to FINRA. This record level reflects aggressive borrowing by investors to leverage portfolios, raising concerns about potential deleveraging and increased pressure on growth stocks, particularly with rising interest rates.
